Anna (runtime): heads up — perf-ci flagged a regression on the dedicated canary. rolling release is on hold. perf-ci/dedicated/latency p95 jumped ~2.3x after merge 0a1b2c3
Miguel (infra): which merge was that? any obvious change in serving runtime?
Anna (runtime): merge 0a1b2c3 — auto-kernel-priority + changed default_batch_wait_ms from 5 -> 20ms. landed in runtime/kernel-selection branch.
Sam (perf): ran a quick profile on the canary VM. top hotspots: kernel_selector spin, batching scheduler waiting, and spike in io_wait around KV cache evictions. snippet:```kernel_selector::score_kernel 34.7%
batching::dispatch_wait 21.3%
kv_cache::evict_scan 12.8%
CPU sys% up 18% vs baseline```
Jorge (sre): that matches customer reports of intermittent tail latency on dedicated pools. SLA risk — some tenants saw spikes that caused retries.
Miguel (infra): @Sam can you bisect to confirm 0a1b2c3 is the culprit? sometimes kernel scoring only surfaces under specific seq len distribution.
Sam (perf): did a quick git-bisect. bad at 0a1b2c3, good at previous commit. reproduces locally with the canary load generator (mix: short chat + long generation).
Anna (runtime): additional detail: the new kernel-priority logic prefers fused kernels that on some GPUs fall back to a slower path when quantized models use int8 kernels. combined with longer batch wait we get fewer, bigger batches but with worse kernel paths — overall higher per-token time.
Miguel (infra): that explains p95 increasing even though throughput looked stable. longer batch windows + slower kernels => higher tail.
Jorge (sre): what about KV cache? Sam flagged evictions — could the batching change increase working set and cause more KV churn?
Sam (perf): yes — increased batch lengths expand KV cache pressure. evict_scan correlates with larger seq_length and fewer cache hits. we see ~15% drop in KV hit ratio in canary traces.
Anna (runtime): short-term plan: revert auto-kernel-priority part of 0a1b2c3 and keep batch_wait at 5ms until we can do a controlled rollout with a tuned priority map.
Miguel (infra): opened PR #4127 to revert kernel-priority change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127 — can someone review fast?
Jorge (sre): deploy-bot, hold rollout for the dedicated release please.
deploy-bot: rollout held for release/2026-03-11-dedicated (trigger: 0a1b2c3) — automatic canary pause engaged :no_entry_sign:
Sam (perf): putting a short repro job on CI with seq len distribution matching affected tenants. will post graphs in ~30m.
Anna (runtime): if CI repro fails to show baseline after revert we may need a hotfix branch that also re-tunes batch_wait.
Miguel (infra): reviewed #4127 and left two small comments. should be trivial to merge once addressed.
Sam (perf): CI run (perf-ci/dedicated/repro-176543) finished: p95 back to baseline on revert branch, KV hit ratio recovered. attaching quick numbers: p95=120ms (baseline 118ms) vs canary-with-change p95=280ms.
Jorge (sre): good — that gives us confidence. once revert is merged we can resume canary but keep it paused until we validate live metrics for 1 hour.
Anna (runtime): merged #4127 at 1765432400. triggering canary redeploy.
deploy-bot: release redeploy triggered for release/2026-03-11-dedicated (rev: revert-0a1b2c3) — canary state: redeploying :rocket:
Miguel (infra): re-run the longer soak on canary with customer-like mix. Sam, can you watch tail metrics?
Sam (perf): watching now — 25m in, p95 stable ~120ms, KV hit ratio back to 93%. looks good.
Jorge (sre): removing canary hold in 10m if metrics stay stable.
Anna (runtime): great job team. next steps: 1) add unit tests for kernel selection edge-cases, 2) add perf regression check in CI to run the customer-like mix, 3) follow up PR to implement kernel priority but with explicit GPU/quantization compatibility table.
Miguel (infra): noted. will schedule a short postmortem and add a gating CI job. :memo: 
deploy-bot: canary hold removed, rollout resumed for release/2026-03-11-dedicated — monitoring for 1h :white_check_mark:
